title: How Multimodal Large Language Models Support Access to Visual Information: A Diary Study With Blind and Low Vision People

bias_targets.methodology: A two-week in-situ diary study capturing 551 interactions from 20 Blind and Low Vision (BLV) participants, followed by qualitative interviews. The study evaluates how standard MLLM training (e.g., RLHF aligned to sighted users' preferences) and overly restrictive safety guardrails disproportionately degrade model utility for BLV users by measuring accuracy, hallucination rates, and inappropriate abstentions during real-world visual assistance tasks.
